method: Primary port and state publications; reporting period kept separate from publication metadata. Source-backed means checked against the cited document, not independent certification of the underlying operations.

exclusions.reason: Vessel/barge table on PDF page 3 labels years 2024/2025 under a Q1 2025/2026 throughput table. Excluded those counts.
Published rounded category totals can differ from their components by one short ton. Use the stated total, not a recomputed value.
2025 review has a conflicting February 2025 body dateline and February 2026 news-index date. Cargo total excluded pending clarification; separate unambiguous rehabilitation release accepted.
Electric crane handover does not establish port-owned equipment or power consumption. The article says the crane is intended for Midwest grain handling.
Utilities are a consolidated expense category. No conversion to electricity kWh, demand, renewable share or port-only consumption.
Selected sites are not completed facilities. No per-site award amounts or completed utility upgrades inferred.
Dated announcements found, but no new port-wide energy measurement accepted.
June 2025 operational booklet surfaced; vessel operating requirements do not establish terminal electricity consumption.
Agenda search results do not establish awards or operating results; no new metric accepted.
2026 location-specific surveys available; no single current port-wide depth inferred.
Regional industrial investment is not evidence of port-owned electricity demand.
